She presented again after 3 years with history of painless progressive swelling in the right side of the neck for the last 1 year. Examination revealed cervical lymph nodes and ascites. This time, a repeat biopsy and immunohistochemistry was suggestive of follicular lymphoma.
The bone marrow aspiration and biopsy revealed normal marrow elements without any evidence of infiltration by lymphoma. She was thus staged as follicular lymphoma stage IV, FLIPI – 2/5, grade 1/2.
This time, a repeat biopsy and immunohistochemistry was suggestive of follicular lymphoma. In view of significant ascites, she was started on chemotherapy with CVP regimen.

After 6 cycles of chemotherapy, she has good partial response and resolution of ascites on repeat imaging with CT. At last follow-up in February 2020 (18 months after chemotherapy), she has maintained the partial response.

summary.text: A 50-year-old woman, diagnosed with follicular lymphoma in 2004 at age 39 and treated with prednisolone and chlorambucil for 5 years until 2009, presented to the authors in March 2015 with slowly progressing neck swelling, low-grade fever and weight loss. Examination showed a 6 × 5 cm right parotid swelling and multiple right-sided lymph nodes; hemoglobin was 10.2 g/dl.

Lymph node and uterine cervix biopsies with immunohistochemistry showed DLBCL, activated B cell type, with a Ki-67 index of 50%; CECT showed parotid swelling, cervical and left inguinal nodes and a uterine cervix mass, and bone marrow was normal. She was staged IIIE with an IPI score of 2/5 and was offered R-CHOP but, because of financial constraints, received 6 cycles of CHOP without rituximab, with very good response and no serious adverse events, then defaulted and was lost to follow-up.

In April 2018 she returned with painless progressive right neck swelling for a year, enlarged right cervical nodes up to 5 × 4 cm and ascites. Hemoglobin was 9.4 g/dl with raised creatinine and uric acid; non-contrast CT showed a right cervical nodal mass involving the parotid, gross ascites and a bulky uterine cervix. Biopsies showed follicular lymphoma grade 1/2 (Ki-67 15 to 20%) in the lymph node and with diffuse areas in the cervix; ascitic cytology and bone marrow were negative. She was staged IV with FLIPI 2/5.

She received 6 cycles of CVP for significant ascites, with good partial response and resolution of ascites on repeat CT; at last follow-up in February 2020 she maintained the partial response, and three-monthly follow-up with yearly or progression-triggered imaging is planned.

article_limitations: The discussion cites literature cases and general statements about follicular lymphoma; none were attributed to the index patient.
Details of the 2004 staging and treatment were not available to the authors.
The neck swelling is described as left-sided in the presentation but the examination describes right-sided findings; retained as a source conflict.
The Fig. 2 caption states splenomegaly while the examination states no hepatosplenomegaly; retained as a source conflict.
Response to CHOP was not assessed by a follow-up scan; the delivered CVP doses are not restated.
Only year or month-level dates are given.
The Fig. 3b caption states no centroblasts in the pictured field while the text reports 5 to 8/hpf; retained as ambiguous.
